headline: Highest risk is medium: whisper can ingest audio files while the other profile is a non-runnable content-writing repo, so only limited pairwise leakage/conflict pathways exist.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction-bridging channel is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable content-writing repository with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b only exposes audio-file input and no clipboard, filesystem read, or MCP path. Without a shared channel, prompt injection from A into B is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies agent_a text into agent_b prompts, reassess as at least low.
IF a shared clipboard or shared filesystem is added, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared prompt channel.
Do not paste agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces, while agent_b touches audio/speech and can read audio files only. The pair does not show a shared workspace or outbound API path, so leakage is limited unless an operator manually moves sensitive audio between them.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared audio directory, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is given sensitive audio files, reassess the data-class exposure.
mitigations: Store audio inputs in separate folders.
Avoid placing sensitive recordings in any shared workspace.
Delete temporary audio files after transcription.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write or mutable-resource capabilities are documented. agent_a has no declared capabilities, and agent_b explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use network egress. That makes direct capability conflict between the pair effectively blocked.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given write or network capabilities, reassess for overlap.
IF agent_b gains filesystem or git write access, reassess for conflict.
mitigations: Do not add shared mutable resources without locking.
requires-engineering: introduce coordination primitives before enabling writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b could treat agent_a-derived text as input only if an operator manually chains them, but agent_a is a static content-writing repo and not a live generator with downstream authority. Because no default action-taking path or verification pipeline is documented, cascading error is possible but narrow.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are manually copied into agent_b transcripts, reassess upward.
IF agent_b is used to act on transcribed content without human review, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before using transcriptions downstream.
Keep transcription outputs separate from decision-making workflows.
requires-engineering: add validation checks before any automated action.

E_compliance.rationale: Compliance exposure is limited to audio/speech data handled by agent_b; agent_a touches no data classes and is a non-runnable repository. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a narrow compliance concern exists if regulated audio is processed.
conditions: IF regulated audio such as PHI or EU PII is processed by agent_b, reassess compliance severity.
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed externally, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated audio to agent_b.
Delete transcripts after use if policy allows.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
